sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing SaaS

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (entered into force 2012)
Panama–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1991)
Panama–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019) and Executive Decree No. 363 de 30 de abril de 2015 govern AML/CFT and PEP due diligence; Ley No. 52 de 27 de octubre de 2016 establishes the mandatory beneficial ownership registry for legal persons and the Public Registry's related enforcement powers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport for each shareholder, director, and proposed officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government passport authority in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority if issued in an Apostille Convention signatory state; otherwise consular legalization at the Panama Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) appointing the Panama resident agent and the directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of each grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by registration with the Public Registry of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate registry extract for each corporate shareholder (UBO piercing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization and, if not already in Spanish, a certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank and professional reference letters, including declaration of source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution and licensed attorney or accountant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and certified Spanish translation; no apostille required for this item unless the compliance file is being legalized for foreign use

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Each shareholder, director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner must be screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions, and Panama's National Prohibition List (Lista Nacional de Personas Prohibidas), with mandatory enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and source-of-funds verification for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) as defined by Law 23/2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) – online name search and reservation services at www.registropublico.gob.pa and at the 'Ventanilla de Nombres' offices
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name may be in Spanish or in any language using the Latin alphabet, must include a corporate denomination such as 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima', and must be transliterated into Latin characters if originating from a non-Latin script. The chosen name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco (requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá)
Seguros or Reaseguros (requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros)
Fideicomiso or Fiduciaria (requires prior regulatory approval)
Fondo de Inversión or Valores (requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores)
Gobierno, Nacional, Municipal or similar terms suggesting public or state status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the public registry rejects or objects to the proposed name, the attorney of record must present a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' before the Dirección General del Registro Público within five (5) business days of notification, attaching a corrected name certificate and renewed search request. Should the reconsideration be denied, the aggrieved party may file an administrative appeal under Ley 38 de 31 de julio de 2000 and, as a final step, an action for 'Nulidad Subjetiva' before the Sala Tercera (Contencioso-Administrativo) of the Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible only where the service provider is a licensed resident agent maintaining a physical street address in Panama that can accept service of process and store corporate records; post-office-box-only addresses or shared mail-forwarding facilities without a doorplate and authorized agent do not satisfy the statutory mandate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this non-regulated SaaS scope: approximately 10% annual probability of an unannounced inspection of the resident agent's registered office by the Public Registry or AML/CFT supervisory authority; direct inspection of the company's operational premises is unlikely absent a complaint trigger or a regulated banking relationship.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and certification (Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre)
Preparation and notarization of Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social), including bilingual drafting
Public Registry incorporation filing and inscription fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the registry's mercantile tariff schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year resident agent and registered office service
AML/KYC compliance package including UBO beneficial ownership filing and PEP screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Duly registered AML compliance officer / licensed professional
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark under Law 23 de 2015

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization processing for foreign corporate and personal documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama and foreign competent authorities

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporation Law of Panama), as amended, Articles 1–21 (formation by public deed), 47–82 (directors and officers); supplemented by Ley No. 47 de 2013 (immobilization and registration of bearer shares) and the Organic Law of the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the customary nominal capital is US$10,000 represented by 10,000 common shares of US$1.00 par value, fully subscribed but without a mandatory escrow account. Shares may be issued as registered or immobilized bearer shares; capital subscription is declared in the public deed and becomes payable at the call of the Board.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS. Unanimously Resolved: (1) The Corporation is validly incorporated under Law No. 32 of 1927; (2) the subscription of 10,000 common shares of US$1.00 par value is accepted and the US$10,000 nominal capital approved as subscribed; (3) the registered office is adopted together with the corporate bylaws; (4) officers are appointed: President, Treasurer, and Secretary, authorized to act singly; (5) officers may open bank accounts, execute tax and registry filings, retain counsel, and sign the municipal Aviso de Operación; (6) pre-incorporation acts for the Corporation's benefit are ratified. This Resolution is immediately effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la Ciudad de Panamá (Notary Public of Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The two founding subscribers appear in person or by attorney-in-fact before a licensed Panamanian notary to execute the Escritura Pública de Constitución. The deed must state the corporate name cleared against the Public Registry records, the registered office address in Panama, a broad corporate purpose expressly covering cloud vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and cybersecurity SaaS, the US$10,000 nominal capital represented by 10,000 shares, the minimum three directors and the statutory officers (President, Treasurer, Secretary), the perpetual duration, and acceptance of registration controls. The notary authenticates the deed, retains the protocol, and issues certified copies for registration.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founding subscribers or corporate resolutions with apostille where a legal entity subscribes
Proposed corporate names (primary plus two alternatives)
Statement of share capital structure and par value
Confirmation of registered office address in Panama
Identification documents of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects drafting defects, the subscribers execute a notarial amendment (Escritura de Aclaración) before filing; if the subscribed entity's resolution is defective, a new duly apostilled corporate resolution is obtained and the deed is re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Public Deed in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary presents a certified copy (testimonio) of the Escritura Pública to the Mercantile Section through the Public Registry's digital filing platform or in person at the registry headquarters. The registry verifies the name, legal form, capital, and formal compliance with Law No. 32 of 1927, assesses the inscription fee on the nominal capital, and issues the registration certificate evidencing the corporate folio. Legal personality and full capacity to contract take effect upon this registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Payment of the registry inscription fee
Certified Spanish translation if any deed clause is in a foreign language
Names and particulars of the three minimum directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice, file a corrective notarial amendment within the peremptory window or submit a written appeal (Recurso de Reconsideración) to the Registro Público; pay any assessed fee deficiency to avoid cancellation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Corporate Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance; SBP-licensed Panamanian banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente with DGI, submitting the registered deed, the designation of the resident legal representative, and the corporate address; upon issuance of the RUC, attend a commercial bank licensed by the Superintendencia de Bancos to open the corporate operating account. The account mandate follows the First Board Resolution and must permit SWIFT wire transfers and Stripe settlement for the SaaS subscription model.
required_dossiers: Identification of the legal representative and appointees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries the file, respond in writing within the stated five-day term and correct the notice; if the bank demands enhanced due diligence on the infosec scope, supply audited financial statements, client contracts, and a sanctions-compliance statement, then re-submit the KYC package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá – Ventanilla Única de la Alcaldía (Single Window of the Municipality of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Aviso de Operación application before commencing local billing or physical operations. The municipality reviews the corporate purpose, the leased office location, the RUC, and the payment of the proportional municipal tax, then issues the annual operating notice. This is the operative commercial license for the SaaS office; no separate cybersecurity-sector statutory license is required for ISIC 6201 in Panama.
required_dossiers: Land-use (uso de suelo) certificate where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality objects to the location or classification, remedy the zoning mismatch and file an amended lease or a corrected use-of-land certificate; pay any assessed surcharge and re-submit through the Ventanilla Única.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Notice, Fire Safety, and Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the operation is an office-based digital service with no industrial emission source, file the Category I Aviso de Operación Ambiental with MiAMBIENTE prior to the commencement of activities. Simultaneously request a fire-safety inspection from the Cuerpo de Bomberos for the issuance of the Certificado de Seguridad covering extinguishers, emergency egress, and electrical panels, and prepare the AGSHT (Análisis de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional) workplace risk assessment required by MITRADEL for occupational health compliance.
required_dossiers: Fire inspection request and building compliance data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MiAMBIENTE upgrades the project to Category II, commission the corresponding Estudio de Impacto Ambiental and follow the public consultation pathway; if the Fire Department flags deficiencies, remediate the physical conditions and schedule a re-inspection with the Cuerpo de Bomberos.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias de Panamá (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas y Actividades Comerciales, in coordination with the Municipalidad de Panamá for the Aviso de Operación
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Notice of Operation) – general commercial operating permit; no sectoral infosec or cybersecurity license is separately required for ISIC 6201 activities in Panama

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Aviso de Operación Ambiental (Environmental Operating Notice) applicable to non-industrial office and knowledge-service operations; full Environmental Impact Study not required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharges permitted; sanitary wastewater must connect to the IDAAN municipal collector or an approved septic system; noise levels must comply with MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0215-2020 office limits; electronic waste from cybersecurity testing hardware must be transferred to MiAMBIENTE-authorized waste handlers under the national solid waste regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá: Certificado de Seguridad (Fire Safety Certificate) confirming extinguishers, emergency egress, signage, and electrical-load safety; MITRADEL: AGSHT workplace risk assessment clearance under the national occupational health and safety rules; Municipalidad de Panamá: structural load and land-use compliance validation for the leased office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of the Republic of Panama; online taxpayer portal SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Tributación en Línea) at www.dgi.gob.pa, including the DGI electronic invoicing module for ITBMS administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Panama S.A.: (1) incorporate by notarized public deed and register the sociedad anónima in the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación (patente) from the Alcaldía of the registered office district; (3) appoint a resident agent and board of directors, then file the SITIO registration for the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC), attaching certified articles of incorporation, registry certificate, and notarized board resolutions; (4) receive the RUC and, where taxable economic activities are exercised in Panamanian territory, the ITBMS sales tax account; (5) enrol in the DGI electronic invoicing system and obtain an accepted advanced digital signature certificate for e-filing and invoice signing. The procedure is normally delegated to a local law or accounting firm acting as resident agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Sociedad Anónima, which is by default an entity-level corporate taxpayer subject to territorial source taxation. Elective statutory mechanisms include: (i) the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying international services, granting income tax and ITBMS benefits; (ii) the Ciudad del Saber regime for eligible technology and research businesses; (iii) the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS fixed-payment regime for annual gross receipts up to PAB 36,000; and (iv) formal asset revaluation or capital basis elections filed with the DGI for income tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available under Panamanian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS), Panama's value added tax equivalent, administered by the DGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Panama establishes no general exemption threshold for business vendors; any person habitually carrying out taxable transfers of goods or services in Panamanian territory must register for ITBMS regardless of turnover. A simplified small-taxpayer regime applies when annual gross receipts do not exceed PAB 36,000 (approximately USD 36,000), substituting the standard monthly returns with a modest quarterly fixed payment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama imposes mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) administered by the DGI for ITBMS taxpayers in staggered phases. Registered taxpayers must issue invoices through DGI-certified software or the DGI portal, sign each invoice with an accepted advanced digital certificate, and transmit the XML/PDF in near real time to the DGI clearance engine, which returns an authorization status (accepted or rejected) together with a fiscal authentication code. The invoice must display a QR code embedding the fiscal hash for buyer-side verification and customs purposes. ERP-to-DGI integration uses a web-services/API standard, and a rejected invoice has no legal validity until corrected and re-submitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Definitive exports of goods are subject to the 0% ITBMS rate, and cross-border services, including cybersecurity SaaS, may be zero-rated when effectively used, consumed, or exploited outside Panama by a nonresident counterparty. The exporter must be registered in the exporters registry, hold an active ITBMS account, issue invoices clearly stating the 0% rate and export destination, and retain a signed contract identifying the nonresident buyer. The supply fails zero-rating if the services are exploited in Panama or rendered to a Panamanian resident, in which case 7% ITBMS applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DUE/SISPA export document) with verified exit date and goods classification
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing definitive export of goods
Commercial invoice issued at 0% ITBMS with export nomenclature and payment terms
Packing list, export permit, or certificate of origin where applicable
Inward remittance certificate issued by a Panamanian licensed bank confirming the entry of foreign currency

For SaaS and digital services: service agreement with the nonresident client, non-residence evidence, and technical records showing the service is consumed abroad (IP addresses, hosting location, subscriber usage logs)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, the DGI and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) jointly verify the documentary file and the actual entry of the export consideration. If the 0% rate is unsupported, the full 7% ITBMS is re-assessed, plus monetary surcharges, monthly default interest, and procedural fines. Under the Código Procesal Tributario (Law 76 of 2019), fraudulent zero-rating or misrepresentation of the export destination can attract penalties between 100% and 300% of the evaded tax and criminal tax-fraud liability for the legal representative, resident agent, and directors. Failure to repatriate the foreign currency within 180 days or to produce the inward remittance certificate reverses the zero-rating retrospectively and triggers unpaid tax, loss of export credits, and inclusion in the DGI targeted audit programme for subsequent periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama maintains no conventional central bank. The banking and foreign-exchange supervisory authority is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), established under Decreto Ley No. 9 de 26 de febrero de 1998. Quasi-central banking and treasury fiscal agency functions are performed by Banco Nacional de Panamá (est. 1904), which acts as the reserve and fiscal agent of the Republic. There is no separate foreign exchange administration or exchange-control tribunal in Panama.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system. The Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a nominal unit pegged at a fixed 1:1 parity to the United States Dollar, and USD is legal tender throughout the Republic pursuant to Decree Law 160 of 1904 and subsequent codification. Both capital and current account transactions are fully convertible with zero prior authorization requirements, no surrender obligations, and no repatriation permits. Profit remittance and dividend distributions are not subject to FX approval gates; practical frictions are limited to AML/CFT documentation, corporate substance evidence, and the applicable Panamanian dividend tax on distributable earnings. For ISIC 6201 cybersecurity SaaS operations, cross-border license and penetration-testing fees constitute export of services and enjoy unrestricted convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: NONE. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation threshold on export receipts. SaaS subscription fees, cloud vulnerability scanning revenues, and penetration-testing service proceeds may be retained in USD, EUR, or any freely chosen currency either onshore or offshore without SBP intervention. The VUCE electronic export declaration is maintained for customs statistics and trade facilitation only and carries no foreign-exchange surrender effect.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational USD Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: RATING: MEDIUM for receivable-collection rails; LOW-to-MEDIUM as a primary treasury settlement spine. Panama enacted Law 223 of 2021 establishing the FinTech Regulatory Sandbox (Innoveting), but licensed EMI participation remains a time-boxed pilot rather than a mature charter regime. Leading offshore digital EMIs and US-domiciled fintech banks typically reject or heavily condition Panamanian Sociedad Anónima entities without a demonstrable US/EU economic nexus. Recommended strategy: sustain a licensed SBP bank USD account as the legal settlement spine, and integrate EMIs such as Stripe, Airwallex, or Wise Platform exclusively for client payment acceptance and invoicing automation. Any payment intermediary collecting Panamanian-origin funds on behalf of PA_CORP becomes subject to SBP payment-system oversight only upon reaching systemically relevant processing volumes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory under SBP Agreement 02-2013 client due diligence rules. All Tier 1 Panamanian banks require at least one director, or the appointed legal representative holding a notarized general power of attorney, to appear in person for the initial KYC interview and wet-ink or digitally certified signature capture. Remote account opening is not practically available for newly formed non-resident holding structures. The attending individual must present a valid passport, the certified public deed of incorporation, the registered agent certificate, and board resolutions reflecting account signatory authority. Video-conference calls may supplement but never fully replace the first in-person identification at most regulated institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-disclosed or bearer-share beneficial ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share certificate inventory; custody letter evidencing immobilization of bearer shares under Law 23 of 2015; SBP UBO declaration forms signed by the ultimate natural-person owner; certified share register and corporate ledger; extracts from the Registro Público de Panamá confirming no bearer instruments remain outstanding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATF grey-list legacy profile and reputational scrutiny over Panamanian S.A. vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current SBP good-standing certificate; audited financial statements issued by a recognized Panamanian CPA firm; corporate tax compliance pipeline report (schema v2.5); board minutes authorizing onboarding; documentary proof of real economic activity including client contracts, cloud infrastructure invoices, payroll records, and office lease or co-working agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of cybersecurity SaaS revenue lacking a transparent source-of-funds trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SaaS subscription agreements and penetration-testing purchase orders; Stripe and wire-transfer settlement statements; cloud provider invoices from AWS, Azure, or equivalent; counterparty IBAN or bank reference evidence for B2B invoices; business continuity documentation listing named enterprise clients in target markets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of nominee directors or professional resident agents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-agent certificate consistent with the Sociedad Anónima legal framework; notarized power of attorney appointing the resident agent solely for service-of-process purposes; engagement letters with the corporate services provider; sworn declaration that the nominee does not independently manage treasury or operating decisions; biographical and professional credentials of the resident agent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute the injection as a direct SWIFT MT103 credit from the contributing shareholder's banking institution to the PA_CORP USD account held at an SBP-licensed bank. Wire memo must state 'Capital contribution' with reference to the public deed number and incorporation date; language such as 'payment for services' is prohibited as it mischaracterizes equity. Evidence bundle comprises the notarized board resolution authorizing the capital increase, updated share register reflecting issuance, certified copy of the public deed, and twelve-month source-of-funds bank statements of the contributing shareholder. Any panama foreign direct investment is exempt from prior SBP approval or FDI screening under Law 41 of 2007. For amounts at or above USD 100,000, the receiving bank will apply enhanced due diligence under Chapter IV of SBP Agreement 02-2013; be prepared to deliver a corporate organizational chart and audited or management-prepared financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary settlement rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for supplier, contractor, and operational vendor payments; (ii) commercial letters of credit advised and confirmed through correspondent banking lines for large infrastructure procurement; and (iii) the domestic Panama Payment House and the Sistema de Pagos de Panamá operated under SBP oversight for same-day USD ACH-equivalent disbursements to Panamanian payroll and local vendors. For ISIC 6201 SaaS treasury flows, typical outlays comprise cloud hosting fees, subcontractor security-research fees, and software license royalties, each payable by MT103 with a purpose description such as 'Cloud infrastructure services' or 'Contractor professional services' referencing the underlying agreement. All USD/EUR and USD/GBP conversions are executed at the servicing bank's desk rate; no regulatory pre-approval applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla USD/EUR and USD/GBP deliverable forwards with tenors up to 12 months executed through SBP-authorized local banks
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on Latin American units such as COP, CLP, and ARS referencing independent international benchmarks
Cross-currency swaps USD/EUR documented under an ISDA Master Agreement for European SaaS subscription flows
FX options strips, collars, and zero-premium structures to hedge material EUR and GBP receivable portfolios
Balboa/USD hedging instruments are functionally redundant because PAB is pegged at fixed 1:1 parity to USD under the dollarized monetary regime

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Anual de las Sociedades Anónimas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and April 15; not tied to incorporation anniversary; no extension available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues administrative surcharges and interest; after 90 days the Registro Público may deny corporate certificates and services, and persistent non-payment (typically two consecutive unpaid annual fees) triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution of the S.A.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar year-end S.A., filed no later than March 31 of the following fiscal year; DGI annual calendar may vary the exact date by RUC ending digit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generates default interest, surcharges of 1% per month or fraction of the tax due, and monetary fines; continued failure may result in DGI collection proceedings, tax liens, and denial of good-standing certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Registry Confirmation / Actualización del Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Beneficial Ownership Registry (RBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April 15 together with the franchise tax filing; ad-hoc update required within 30 calendar days after any share transfer or beneficial ownership change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Law 23 of 2015 ranging from USD 500 to USD 5,000 for late, incomplete, or inaccurate filings; repeated breaches may lead to suspension of corporate rights and administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panama S.A. is required to present audited financial statements when annual gross Panamanian-source revenue exceeds USD 1,500,000, or when total assets exceed USD 3,000,000, or when the DGI orders an audit based on business volume, risk, or regulated status. Cybersecurity/SaaS entities below these thresholds are not subject to a mandatory statutory audit unless required by shareholders, investors, lenders, or DGI request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted and endorsed by the Contador General de la Nación; SMEs may apply IFRS for SMEs in accordance with DGI Administrative Rules and Panama Accounting Regulation No. 201-04.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each S.A. must maintain complete and current UBO information and file it through its registered agent with the Registro Público's Beneficial Ownership Registry (RBF). The annual confirmation is integrated with the franchise tax renewal cycle and must precisely reflect shareholding percentages after any transfer. A share transfer must be recorded and submitted to the RBF within 30 calendar days to be valid against third parties; the registered agent is legally responsible for collecting and filing updated UBO data. The confirmation is required even if no share movement occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores y Oficiales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 700 per year for a compliant resident agent and registered office service provider; additional notarial or government auxiliary charges are not included.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 – USD 4,500 per engagement for a certified audit of a cybersecurity SaaS S.A.; USD 600 – USD 1,200 for a review or compilation prepared for internal or lender purposes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source exemption: 0% on qualifying foreign-source revenue (e.g., cybersecurity SaaS licensing and cloud penetration-testing services contracted, rendered, and economically utilized outside Panama); SEM regime under Law 41 of 2007 (Multinational Headquarters Sede de Empresa Multinacional) imposes a 5% preferential ISR on qualifying cross-border HQ service income; Ciudad del Saber (Law 28 of 2006) licenses can grant full income tax exemption for technology companies for up to 20 years; statutory deduction of 1.5x on salaries for new Panamanian employment in services exports; accelerated depreciation on software, server, and R&D equipment; VAT/ITBMS exemption on exported services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 - Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas (Sociedades), filed electronically via the DGI e-Tax 2.0 portal (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa); taxpayers must hold an active RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and use the DGI digital signature (Firma Digital).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly advance income tax payments (pagos a cuenta).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year S.A., no later than 31 March of the following year. Quarterly advances of the minimum tax are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December for taxpayers with annual gross income exceeding PAB 1,500,000 or net assets exceeding PAB 3,000,000 (USD-peg 1:1).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A - RUC and Identification Data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, RUC, fiscal year, aviso de operación number, authorized share capital, economic activity code (ISIC 6201 / CIIU 6201), local registered agent (agente residente) details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be identified by name, passport number, and country of tax residence; the alternate director or resident agent shall certify the beneficial ownership schedule for DGI inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Line 1 - Ingresos Brutos (Gross Revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide gross income derived during the fiscal year, including SaaS subscription fees, penetration-testing service fees, and software license charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross receipts; separately identify foreign-source items rather than omitting them, as the DGI cross-matches e-invoicing (Factura Electrónica) and payment-rail data from Stripe and wire transfers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Line 2 - Ingresos de Fuente Panameña (Panama-Source Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue attributable to activities performed, contracts executed, and services economically consumed within Panamanian territory; this portion is subject to ISR at the headline 25% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SaaS vendors should conservatively exclude receipts where the customer, server infrastructure, and contract law are foreign; the DGI rejects blanket exclusions without a documented 'nexo territorial' (territorial nexus) analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Line 3 - Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera (Foreign-Source Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt revenue derived from services rendered entirely abroad; must be traceable to contracts entered into abroad, foreign bank accounts, and foreign delivery of digital services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the annexed 'Anexo / Declaración Jurada de Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera' and segregate these profits in the 'Reserva de Utilidades por Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera' before any dividend distribution to preserve the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, salaries, rent, cybersecurity R&D expenses, depreciation, software amortization, and financing costs directly attributable to Panamanian-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses allocated to foreign-source exempt income are non-deductible; foreign-owned S.A.s must submit transfer-pricing support for any related-party cost allocation to avoid a 25% add-back and 40% penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D, Line 14 - Renta Neta Gravable (Net Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net taxable income after statutory deductions, loss carryforwards, and inflation adjustments; the result is the base for the 25% ISR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is limited to 5 tax years; losses generated by foreign-source activities cannot offset Panamanian-source taxable income; AMT check applies: 4.16% of gross Panamanian-source revenue where it exceeds book-computed ISR (Alternative Minimum Tax - IMAS).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D, Line 17 - ISR Causado (25% Corporate Tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Headline 25% statutory rate applied to the net taxable Panamanian-source income line.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the reduced 5% SEM rate only if the S.A. holds a valid SEM registry; the standard 25% rate otherwise applies to any Panamanian-source profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E, Line 20 - Créditos (Credits and Advance Payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for quarterly advance payments (pagos a cuenta), income tax withheld by third parties, and the 10% advance dividend tax already paid on retained Panamanian-source earnings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders holding more than 10% are entitled to the foreign-tax credit only where a DTA applies; attach the DGI-approved treaty-relief notice to reduce the dividend WHT credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section F, Line 23 - Saldo a Pagar / A Favor (Final Balance Due)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable after credits, or the refundable balance from excess advance payments; payment via the DGI bank network or e-Tax 2.0 digital payment module.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Balances due must be settled no later than the 31 March deadline; deferral accrues monthly interest of 1% (approx. 12% p.a.) plus a 5%-per-month surcharge capped at 50% of the unpaid ISR.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction, capped at 50% of the tax due; minimum administrative fine of PAB 50 for late or non-filing of a nil return; statutory interest at the legal rate (10-12% per annum) on unpaid ISR; failure to file for two consecutive years can lead to suspension of the RUC and the 'Aviso de Operación', blocking Stripe and bank wire settlements; repeated non-compliance triggers criminal tax fraud sanctions (Código Fiscal Article 704; Código Penal Articles 338 and 339).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The 10% dividend WHT is a final withholding obligation of the Panamanian S.A. on any distribution of Panamanian-source retained earnings. Dividends sourced from documented foreign-source reserves are exempt with no withholding. To claim DTA relief: (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the foreign shareholder's tax authority, valid for the calendar year; (2) file the DGI treaty-relief application (Formulario de Solicitud de Aplicación de Tratado en Materia de Doble Tributación) in e-Tax 2.0 with the S.A.'s digital signature; (3) execute a Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming the ultimate recipient and a 10%-or-greater shareholding for the reduced 5% treaty dividend rate; (4) receive a DGI advance ruling or acceptance notice before applying the reduced rate at source; (5) retain the TRC, board resolution declaring the dividend, and ownership registry (Registro de Accionistas) for a minimum of 6 years. Treaty-reduced dividend rates typically range from 0% to 10% (e.g., 5% for 10%+ holdings under the Spain, Netherlands, UK, Singapore, Mexico, and Korea DTAs).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory final withholding on outbound royalties, technical assistance fees, and interest payments derived from Panamanian sources is 12.5% for non-residents (Código Fiscal Article 733); statutory rate for interest on bank loans is also 12.5% when paid to a foreign lender. DTA caps generally reduce interest to 5-10% (e.g., Korea and Singapore 5%, Mexico 10%) and royalties to 0-10% (e.g., Netherlands and UK 2.5%-5% for copyright-equivalent SaaS/IP licenses; Korea 2.5%-10%; Singapore 5%). The S.A. must apply the treaty rate at source only after submitting the TRC and the DGI treaty-relief notice; the payer is severally liable for the under-withheld amount plus penalties if the treaty protocol is not followed. Conversely, SaaS subscription receipts from foreign clients routed through foreign payment providers are foreign-source and exempt from Panamanian WHT, provided the territorial-nexus evidence is maintained.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 2,000,000 (Balboa 2 million, equivalent to USD 2 million due to the 1:1 peg) of aggregate annual related-party cross-border transactions triggers the mandatory preparation of the Local File and Transfer Pricing Report under Law 365 of 14 December 2023 and DGI implementing regulations; Master File is obligatory when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds PAB 750,000,000 (USD 750 million). Documentation must be filed as an annex to the Formulario 101 at the filing deadline; administrative penalties apply for non-filing even if no adjustment arises.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but the doctrine is enforced through territorial-nexus rules and SEM licensing under Law 41 of 2007. The DGI, under the BEPS-aligned reforms of Law 133 of 2022 and Law 365 of 2023, may deny the foreign-source exemption of a S.A. that cannot evidence: (i) physical presence (office/lease), (ii) Panamanian employees or local subcontractors, (iii) board meetings and decision-making in Panama, (iv) local bank accounts, and (v) contracts executed with commercial substance. A 'shell' S.A. with nominee officers and no operational footprint will be re-characterized as fully Panamanian-resident, subjecting worldwide income to the 25% ISR, the 10% advanced dividend tax, and 10% dividend WHT, irrespective of the foreign client location.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Misclassification of Digital Services (Código Fiscal Articles 700, 704, 754; Código Penal Articles 338-339)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately booking Panama-origin SaaS revenue (local clients, local support, local servers) as foreign-source, or fabricating foreign reserve accounts and advisory contracts to reduce the 25% ISR and the 10% dividend tax; understating gross receipts from Stripe and wire-transfer rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, a fine of PAB 25,000 to PAB 100,000, and recapture of all evaded ISR plus monthly default interest (approx. 12% p.a.) and a 50% surcharge on unpaid taxes; loss of the foreign-source reserve privilege; publication of the taxpayer on the DGI blacklist and revocation of the Aviso de Operación.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the resident agent, and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable under Law 133 of 2022 veil-piercing rules when the company is used as a conduit for evasion; the DGI may obtain a court-ordered impedimento de salida (travel ban) for tax debts exceeding PAB 50,000; assets of the directors can be attached for civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Entity - Failure of Economic Substance and Territorial Nexus
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the S.A. with nominal capital, nominee directors, no Panamanian office, no payroll, and routing all cybersecurity SaaS contracts through foreign shell entities solely to claim 0% foreign-source exemption without real business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI re-characterization of the entire worldwide income as Panamanian-source, retroactive assessment for up to 3 fiscal years of 25% ISR plus the 10% advance dividend tax, monthly default interest of 1%, and a surcharge of up to 50% of the total omitted tax; cancellation of the SEM license, if fraudulently obtained, and disqualification from re-entry for 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court can pierce the corporate veil and hold directors and the resident agent personally liable for the full tax deficiency where the structure is a sham; personal liability extends to unpaid withholding taxes (the 12.5% royalty and interest WHT) and the 10% dividend WHT; directors face travel bans and criminal proceedings for false affidavits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Anti-Money-Laundering Violations (Law 23 of 2015; UAF Resolutions; Código Penal Article 254)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Stripe or wire-transfer payments from sanctioned persons, ransomware groups, or unverified high-risk counterparties without adequate KYC/CDD, transaction monitoring, or beneficial-ownership verification; converting crypto-ransomware proceeds into commercial SaaS invoices; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 imposes fines of PAB 10,001 to PAB 1,000,000 per violation, suspension or revocation of the Aviso de Operación and bank accounts, and in serious cases, the crime of money laundering (Código Penal Article 254) carries 5 to 10 years of imprisonment plus a fine of up to PAB 1,000,000; additional risk under OFAC and international sanctions for dealing with designated ransomware actors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for AML program failures; the Superintendencia de Bancos and UAF can impose travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification from holding corporate officer positions in Panama; personal criminal liability attaches where directors knew or recklessly disregarded the illicit origin of subscription deposits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance (Law 365 of 2023; OECD TRG)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing cross-border related-party transactions (e.g., management fees, IP royalties, R&D cost-sharing, or intercompany loans with the foreign parent or a BVI tech-IP holding co) above the PAB 2,000,000 threshold without preparing the Local File/Master File, or applying a non-arm's-length margin below the tested profit spread.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative adjustment to the arm's-length margin with a 40% penalty on the primary TP adjustment, plus monthly default interest; failure to timely submit the TP documentation attracts an autonomous fine of PAB 2,500 to PAB 10,000 per annual return; repeated non-compliance elevates the case to the DGI Special Audit Unit and can trigger mutual agreement procedures (MAP) revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed fraudulent TP certificates or who instructed under-pricing of exported SaaS services are jointly liable for the resulting tax deficiency after veil-piercing; the DGI can obtain court orders freezing personal bank accounts of directors and refusing exit permits for penalties exceeding PAB 50,000.
